correctness.rationale: Write the inner conjunction as B=¬□a∧¬¬a. On the two-world chain with universal R, a false at the bottom and true at the top, every box test for a sees the bottom and every order test for ¬a sees the top; therefore □a and ¬a both fail everywhere, B holds everywhere, and □B witnesses the failure of ¬□B at the root. Universal R satisfies both confluences and is reflexive and transitive; the valuation is upward closed. On a one-world IS4 frame, box is identity and intuitionistic negation is Boolean, so B is false for both valuations and F is true. On a singleton IK4 frame empty R is transitive and confluent vacuously, makes □B true independently of a, and refutes F. A refutation needs at least one world. These cases prove the exact minima under the cited semantics.
residual_risks: No claim for serial IK4 variants or for other formulas; no computational or formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: The example was independently motivated by a real looping failure mode in proof search. The exact IS4 size is a useful minimal benchmark: the loop occurs even when just two worlds suffice and a one-world closure would be invalid. The IK4 singleton provides a clean semantic control in which removing reflexivity removes even that one-world obstruction. The combination separates intrinsic countermodel size from the size behavior of the naive construction without claiming a general bound.
residual_risks: The singleton IK4 observation is routine in isolation. Value rests on the exact optimum of a named loop benchmark, not on novelty of vacuous box truth or improvement of the published decision procedure.
